registration: Local frozen exploratory follow-up, not external preregistration. V1 outcomes already known.
question: Does language-matched scoring benefit survive fully crossing independent key and search-seed variation?
sources: Same six reviewed public passages from three works as v1; first excerpts excluded unchanged.
keyDesign: Reuse all 30 independent v1 ciphertext/key fixtures unchanged to isolate crossing search seeds, not introduce a new key population. Five keys per passage.
primaryOutcome: Top-candidate normalized Levenshtein edit error; positional/key error and exact recovery secondary.
comparison: Matched minus baseline and matched minus mean of BOTH mismatched models, within identical ciphertext/seed/solver.
reporting: All runs and failures. Overall, work, passage, key index and search seed. Also per-ciphertext seed variance and within-passage variance of key means. No significance or best-seed selection.
limits: Public previously evaluated sample; not blind or fresh holdout.
Six passages in only three works; seeds/keys are not independent documents.
No modern same-language baseline: cannot isolate historical orthography benefits.
No tuning, changed scoring, changed initialization or higher budget.
Latin annealing exception known before this follow-up.
Beam deterministic: run once per key/scorer, not five duplicate seed conditions.
repositoryStatus: Existing working tree changes were present; copied input hashes, not HEAD alone, identify experiment bytes.
